body.title: docs(skills): expand glab-stack guidance for non-interactive reorder and infer
body.description:
## Description

Follow-up to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4267, which made `glab stack reorder` and `glab stack infer` usable without a TTY. That MR updated the bundled `glab-stack` skill, but agents following the skill could still get stuck or leave GitLab out of sync. This MR fills those gaps:

- **`infer` needs `--name` when no stack is active.** Without it, `infer --all` fails with "no stack found and no TTY available". Rule 6 now says so, and there's a new quick-reference row.
- **`reorder` only rebases locally.** Rule 5 now says to run `glab stack sync` afterwards to force-push.
- **Reorder conflict recovery.** A new section covers `git rebase --continue` followed by `glab stack reorder --continue` or `--abort`. Both commands are also in the quick reference.
- **Branch-list rules for `reorder`.** List every branch exactly once, the first branch sits on the base branch, and commit or stash tracked changes first.
- **Wording.** `reorder` and `infer` without the new arguments now "hang or fail without a TTY", and the skill description mentions inferring a stack from commits.

## Related Issues

Related to #8658

## How has this been tested?

Docs-only change to `SKILL.md`. The `validate-skills` and markdownlint hooks pass, as do the `internal/commands/skills` tests.

body.title: fix(note): keep a piped body when --attach is set
body.description:
## Description

With `--attach`, `glab mr note create`, `glab mr note draft create`, `glab mr note update`, `glab mr note draft update`, `glab issue note`, and `glab incident note` never read the body from stdin. A piped body was silently dropped and the note held only the attachment links.

All four MR commands and the issuable note command gated `NoteBodyFromStdinOrEditor` on `len(attach) == 0`. The new `cmdutils.SkipNoteBody` narrows that to the two cases that need it:

- `--attach -`: the attachment claims standard input.
- An interactive terminal: an attachment-only note must not open the editor.

Update commands now replace the existing body with a piped one and append the links. With empty stdin they keep appending the links to the existing body, as before. Help text is updated and `docs/source/` regenerated with `make gen-docs`. The bundled `glab` skill now covers `--attach` with piped bodies and its stdin pitfalls.

## Behavior change

`--attach` is experimental, but scripts may rely on the old "does not read stdin" behavior. With `--attach <file>` and no `--message`, standard input that is not a terminal is now read as the body:

- A pipe that stays open makes the command wait until it closes.
- In a `while read` loop, the first call consumes the rest of the loop's input as its body.
- To post only the attachment (or keep the existing body on `update`) from a script, redirect standard input from `/dev/null`. `--message ""` does not help, because an empty message counts as no message.

The help text of every affected command says this.

## Related Issues

Resolves #8720

## How has this been tested?

- New unit tests: `SkipNoteBody` table test; non-TTY piped body + `--attach <file>` for `mr note create`, `mr note update`, `mr note draft create`, `mr note draft update`, and `issue note`; empty stdin + `--attach <file>` posts only the reference, and keeps the existing body on `mr note update`. Existing tests for append-to-existing on update, `--attach -`, and attachment-only notes on a terminal still pass.
- Against a local GDK, every command was run with the pre-change and the new binary, and each note body was read back from the API:

| Command | Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mr note create` | body piped + `--attach file` | link only | body + link |
| `mr note create` | empty stdin + `--attach file` | - | link only |
| `mr note create` | PNG piped + `--attach -` | - | link only (image uploaded) |
| `mr note create` | terminal + `--attach file` | - | link only, no editor |
| `mr note update` | body piped / empty stdin | - | replaces / appends to existing |
| `mr note draft create` | body piped + `--attach file` | link only | body + link |
| `mr note draft update` | body piped / empty stdin | - | replaces / appends to existing |
| `issue note` | body piped + `--attach file` | link only | body + link |
| `incident note` | body piped + `--attach file` | - | body + link |

- The documented script behavior, also on the local GDK:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `sleep 6 \| glab mr note create 1 --attach f` | glab takes 6.3s, link only |
| same with `</dev/null` | glab takes 0.3s, link only |
| `while read` loop over 3 files | 1 note, the remaining paths become its body |
| same loop with `</dev/null` | 3 notes, link only each |
| `mr note update` / `draft update` with `</dev/null` | existing body kept, link appended |

body.title: ci(snap): fail edge release job on upload errors again
body.description:
The Snap Store granted the `dot-kube-config` personal-files declaration, so edge uploads pass automated review again. This drops the temporary `allow_failure: true` on `snapcraft_release_edge`, so real upload failures are visible again. The `retry:` block stays for transient store errors.

Example passing edge release with the plug: https://dashboard.snapcraft.io/snaps/glab/revisions/7121/ (`1.128.0-12-g2823efa`, released to `latest/edge`). Uploaded by `snapcraft_release_edge` in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/jobs/17722835743, which logs `Revision 7121 created for 'glab' and released to 'latest/edge'`.

Relates to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8304

body.title: test(api): pin the Duo Agent Platform auth contract
body.description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Adds a contract test for how GitLab Duo Agent Platform workloads authenticate glab.

Those workloads install the glab version pinned in `gitlab-org/gitlab` and set it up without `glab auth login`:

- `GlabSetup#config_file_command` (`ee/lib/gitlab/duo_workflow/glab_setup.rb`) writes `config.yml` with `is_oauth2: 'true'`, `client_id: bypass`, and no `token`.
- `StartWorkflowService` (`ee/app/services/ai/duo_workflows/start_workflow_service.rb`) passes the Doorkeeper OAuth token through `GITLAB_TOKEN`, together with `GLAB_IS_OAUTH2=true`, inside a CI job.

glab 1.111.0 started sending that token as `Private-Token` (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8482). Nothing caught it automatically. It was found by hand while bumping the pin (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/247970). The monolith specs don't run the binary, and `TestNewClientFromConfig_OAuthFlagProvenance` covers the flag combinations in general rather than this setup.

Renovate now opens the pin bumps on a weekly schedule (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/frontend/renovate-gitlab-bot/-/merge_requests/1771). So this test reproduces DAP's config and environment and asserts glab sends `Authorization: Bearer` to the right API base URL. It covers four host setups: default port, non-default port, relative URL root, and HTTP.

## How to set up and validate locally

```shell
go test ./internal/api/ -run DuoAgentPlatformContract -count=1 -v
```

To check that it catches the 1.111.0 regression, make `isEnvironmentOAuth2` always false in `internal/api/client.go`. Every case then fails with `Private-Token` instead of `Authorization`.
